2022 · Internal tools·CMS

App Review Platform

Ground-up rebuild of Wix App Market’s internal review platform that shortened review cycles.

Presentation mode ↗
TL;DR

The problemI planned and rebuilt a stale internal app review tool with a clearer structure and the features reviewers were missing.

ProcessI started with interviews and by shadowing Account Managers as they ran reviews, then tested the redesign with them in a bug hunt before launch.

The resultReview cycles got shorter, and the team has used the tool and added features to it since the 2022 launch.

The problemReviews couldn't keep up with submissions

Account Managers who review apps for the Wix App MarketWix App Market is a marketplace where third-party developers publish apps for Wix site owners. Developers manage their apps through the Wix Developer Center, a dashboard covering submissions, reviews, payouts, and analytics. wrote their reviews in different tools: some used Google Docs, others used Sheets. The internal review tool was stuck in a loop: it wasn't updated, so no one used it, and with no one using it, it never got updated.

More and more apps were being submitted, and the review process had no clear structure. Reviews were inconsistent and slow, with many review cycles.

The problems in the review process

Many review rounds per submission

No shared history

No visibility into what changed between submissions

No consistent handoff between the reviewers

Manual reviews with no shared structure

No overview of status or reviewers

ApproachWatching how reviewers work

Research process

Walkthroughs. Went through the old tool with Account Managers.

Shadowing. Watched them run real reviews.

Audit. Went through the Docs and Sheets they used instead.

Analytics. Time to publish and resubmissions.

Pain points

A confusing UI, not matching WixWix is a website builder and development platform used by millions of businesses and creators worldwide. design system

A broken workflow. Every account manager wrote in their own way.

No shared history. Hand-offs between account managers were hard.

Rechecking apps after the 2nd submission took a lot of time.

Design principles

We decided on three rules.

01

Make every step traceable

Every comment is logged, and the app's activity is tracked from draft to publish for easier tracking and handoff.

Accountability
02

Highlight app changes

A before and after view lets reviewers focus on changes and not review the app all over again.

Velocity
03

Still keep the account manager in control

Blockers disable publishing, and publishing or declining an app is deliberate - this was a request from the account managers.

Control

SolutionDivided the tool to four product areas

App directory and queue

Browse, filter and assign every app across all review stages.

Fixing weak information architecture

App page

One app's log history, team and statuses in a single view.

Simplifying the general workflow.

Review workspace (NEW)

Built from scratch to replace the Google Doc manual reviews, with comments the old tool never had.

This way reviews will be consistent.

Review team management

Role-based access: the manager assigns apps and oversees reviews, Account Managers review, viewers see the details and the report.

Improving handoff between reviewers

Apps directory and review queue

The full marketplace directory, across all stages. Click any image to see it bigger.

App page

Submission history, team notes, and current status

Review workflow

Commenting, flagging issues, and submitting the review in one place

Publish flow

The last step before publishing to the marketplace

Team management and roles

Role-based access for the review team

Delivery & challengesWorking with the team

Process

My partners. Account Managers team and lead, a PM, content writer and developers.

Weekly syncs with Account Management to align on scope and surface edge cases early.

Working in parallel. Development started working alongside product work, so we also synced with them regularly.

A bug hunt with the Account Managers before launch.

Challenges

The platform had to be better than the workaround reviewers already used - without making them relearn how they work.

Showing app changes (Diffs) in a readable way

Sending the review still happened in a separate Wix platform, because the two systems were not connected.

Impact & next stepsFrom a stale tool to the new platform

The team stopped working in Google Docs and moved their reviews into the platform, where anyone with permission can follow an app's full history.

"I like the fact that I can transfer past comments to the new report, it really saves time"

Shorter cycles

Reviews took fewer rounds, and each round was shorter.

Still active

In use since the 2022 launch, and features are still being added.

Keeps improving

The team added filters and a premium marker themselves, work that used to need a developer.

Next steps

Send reports from the tool, and add analytics on reviewer comments.
